Repo: /dayjs (dayjs JS date library, jest, node_modules installed). Work ONLY inside /dayjs. No internet. Other subagents are concurrently editing src/plugin/timezone/index.js, src/plugin/weekYear/index.js and src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js — do NOT touch those files. You may create/delete your own temp test file /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_nl.test.js.

BUG TO FIX (src/locale/nl.js): the Dutch locale's `ordinal` is currently `ordinal: n => `${n}.``, which produces '1.', '2.', ... '31.'. The expected behaviour (the repo aims to be a drop-in Moment.js replacement and its own locale tests compare dayjs against moment) is the Dutch ordinal used by moment: '1ste', '2e', '3e', ..., '8ste', ..., '20ste', ...

STEP 1 (evidence, do this first): read /dayjs/node_modules/moment/locale/nl.js and report the exact `ordinal` function it defines (and its ordinalParse regex if any). Also read /dayjs/src/locale/nl.js.

STEP 2: change ONLY the `ordinal` entry of /dayjs/src/locale/nl.js so that it reproduces moment's nl ordinal exactly, adapted to dayjs's calling convention. dayjs calls `locale.ordinal(dayOfMonth)` for the 'Do' token and `locale.ordinal(weekNumber, 'W')` for the 'wo' token (see src/plugin/advancedFormat/index.js). So the dayjs signature is (number, period). If moment's nl ordinal is
    function (number) { return number + (number === 1 || number === 8 || number >= 20 ? 'ste' : 'e'); }
then write:
  ordinal: (number, period) => {
    switch (period) {
      case 'W':
        return `${number}e`
      default:
        return `${number}${number === 1 || number === 8 || number >= 20 ? 'ste' : 'e'}`
    }
  },
but FIRST verify the exact moment logic from the file and mirror it precisely (do not guess). If moment's nl ordinal already equals `${n}.`, do NOT edit; report that instead.

STEP 3 VERIFY:
1. Write /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_nl.test.js that loads the nl locale for both libraries (import nl from '../src/locale/nl'; dayjs.locale(nl, null, true); moment.locale('nl')) and for i = 1..31 compares dayjs(`2018-01-${i}`).format('Do') with moment(`2018-01-${i}`).format('Do'), printing every pair and every mismatch. Run: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/zz_tmp_nl.test.js --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -60
2. Run: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/locale --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -30 to make sure the locale tests (including test/locale/keys.test.js) still pass.
3. Run the FULL suite before and after your edit (cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -20). Baseline in this container (TZ=UTC) is 56 suites / 524 tests all passing; report any test that passed before and fails after.
4. DELETE /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_nl.test.js afterwards and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only src/locale/nl.js modified by you.

FINAL REPORT: moment's nl ordinal source, the exact diff applied, the Do 1..31 comparison output (all 31 pairs), the locale-test result, the full-suite result before/after, and confirmation the temp file was deleted.

Repo: /dayjs (dayjs JS date library, jest, node_modules installed). Work ONLY inside /dayjs. No internet. Other subagents are concurrently editing src/plugin/timezone/index.js, src/plugin/weekYear/index.js, src/plugin/customParseFormat/index.js and src/locale/nl.js — do NOT touch those. You may create/delete your own temp test file /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_duration.test.js.

BUG TO FIX (src/plugin/duration/index.js): the `unitToMS` map is missing a `milliseconds` entry:

const unitToMS = {
  years: MILLISECONDS_A_YEAR,
  months: MILLISECONDS_A_MONTH,
  days: MILLISECONDS_A_DAY,
  hours: MILLISECONDS_A_HOUR,
  minutes: MILLISECONDS_A_MINUTE,
  seconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND,
  weeks: MILLISECONDS_A_WEEK
}

Because of that, `dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds')` (and `dayjs.duration(100, 'ms')`, and `.add(100, 'milliseconds')`) computes `input * undefined` = NaN, so the resulting duration is invalid (its toISOString() is 'P0D' / NaN). Add the missing entry so the map reads:

const unitToMS = {
  years: MILLISECONDS_A_YEAR,
  months: MILLISECONDS_A_MONTH,
  days: MILLISECONDS_A_DAY,
  hours: MILLISECONDS_A_HOUR,
  minutes: MILLISECONDS_A_MINUTE,
  seconds: MILLISECONDS_A_SECOND,
  milliseconds: 1,
  weeks: MILLISECONDS_A_WEEK
}

Make ONLY that change. Do not modify any other file.

VERIFY:
1. Write /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_duration.test.js that checks, for units ['milliseconds','ms','millisecond','second','seconds','minute','minutes','hour','hours','day','days','week','weeks','month','months','year','years'] and values [1, 100, 1000, 1500, 61, 3600, 86400], that `dayjs.duration(v, u).toISOString()` equals `moment.duration(v, u).toISOString()` (moment is available as `import moment from 'moment'`), printing every mismatch as `unit | value | dayjs=.. | moment=..` and the total mismatch count. Also check `dayjs.duration(100, 'milliseconds').asMilliseconds() === 100`, `dayjs.duration(1500, 'milliseconds').milliseconds() === 500`, `dayjs.duration(100, 'ms').toISOString() === 'PT0.1S'`, and that `dayjs.duration(100).toISOString() === 'PT0.1S'` and `dayjs.duration(1000).toISOString() === 'PT1S'` still hold. Run: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/zz_tmp_duration.test.js --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -60
2. Run: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/plugin/duration.test.js --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -20 (all pre-existing duration tests must still pass).
3. Run the FULL suite before and after your edit: cd /dayjs && npx jest --coverage=false 2>&1 | tail -20. Baseline in this container (TZ=UTC) is 56 suites / 524 tests all passing; report any test that passed before and fails after.
4. DELETE /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_duration.test.js afterwards and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows src/plugin/duration/index.js modified only by the expected change.

FINAL REPORT: the exact diff, the mismatch counts before/after, the duration suite result, the full-suite result before/after, and confirmation the temp file was deleted.

You are working in the dayjs repository at /dayjs (JavaScript date library, jest tests, node_modules installed). Another subagent is concurrently editing ONLY /dayjs/src/plugin/timezone/index.js — you must NOT edit any source file. You may only create and later delete your own temporary test file /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_z.test.js. Do not use the internet.

GOAL: find out exactly how dayjs's timezone plugin output diverges from moment-timezone (the reference implementation used by this repo's own tests) for the `Z` / `ZZ` format tokens, so we can locate a bug in src/plugin/timezone/index.js.

STEP 1: run `date`, `node -e "console.log(process.env.TZ, new Date().getTimezoneOffset(), new Date().toString())"` and report the container's current date, TZ and local UTC offset.

STEP 2: create /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_z.test.js with a differential test. Content sketch (adapt as needed):

import moment from 'moment-timezone'
import dayjs from '../src'
import utc from '../src/plugin/utc'
import timezone from '../src/plugin/timezone'
dayjs.extend(utc)
dayjs.extend(timezone)

const zones = ['America/New_York', 'America/Los_Angeles', 'Europe/London', 'Europe/Paris', 'Asia/Tokyo', 'Asia/Kolkata', 'Australia/Sydney', 'Pacific/Auckland', 'America/St_Johns', 'Pacific/Chatham', 'UTC']
const instants = ['2014-06-01T12:00:00Z', '2014-12-01T12:00:00Z', '2012-03-11T06:59:59Z', '2012-11-04T05:30:00Z', '2014-06-01T12:00:00.123Z', '2014-06-01T12:00:00.500Z', '2020-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2014-06-01T00:00:00Z']

it('diff', () => {
  const rows = []
  zones.forEach((z) => {
    instants.forEach((i) => {
      const d = dayjs(i).tz(z)
      const m = moment(i).tz(z)
      const fields = ['format', 'formatZ', 'formatZZ', 'utcOffset', 'valueOf']
      const dv = [d.format(), d.format('Z'), d.format('ZZ'), d.utcOffset(), d.valueOf()]
      const mv = [m.format(), m.format('Z'), m.format('ZZ'), m.utcOffset(), m.valueOf()]
      fields.forEach((f, k) => {
        if (dv[k] !== mv[k]) rows.push(`${z} | ${i} | ${f} | dayjs=${dv[k]} | moment=${mv[k]}`)
      })
    })
  })
  console.log('MISMATCHES:\n' + (rows.length ? rows.join('\n') : 'none'))
  expect(true).toBe(true)
})

Also add a second `it` that does the same for wall-clock string parsing: for each zone and for strings ['2014-06-01 12:00', '2012-11-04 01:00:00', '2012-03-11 02:30:00', '2014-12-01 12:00'], compare dayjs.tz(s, z) against moment.tz(s, z) on format(), format('Z'), utcOffset(), valueOf().

Run it with: cd /dayjs && npx jest test/zz_tmp_z.test.js --coverage=false 2>&1 | head -200
Then run the same file under several TZs and report the mismatch lists for each:
  TZ=UTC npx jest test/zz_tmp_z.test.js --coverage=false
  TZ=Europe/London npx jest test/zz_tmp_z.test.js --coverage=false
  TZ=America/New_York npx jest test/zz_tmp_z.test.js --coverage=false
  TZ=Pacific/Auckland npx jest test/zz_tmp_z.test.js --coverage=false

STEP 3: narrow down. For every mismatch you find, print the intermediate values: for the instance, print d.$offset, d.$u, d.valueOf(), d.toDate().toISOString(), and for moment print m.utcOffset(), m.valueOf(). Also print `dayjs().utcOffset()` (the localUtcOffset captured at plugin load) and `new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`.

STEP 4: DELETE /dayjs/test/zz_tmp_z.test.js when done (verify with `ls /dayjs/test`).

FINAL REPORT: the container date/TZ; the exact mismatch lines (dayjs vs moment) per TZ; the diagnosis of which expression in src/plugin/timezone/index.js produces the wrong offset; and any case where dayjs and moment agree. Be precise and include raw output.
